description: baseline 1 with the post-change file only, no diff

cases.note: The '^' anchor was removed from parseRegExp, so parse() now extracts a size/unit pair from anywhere in the string. Inputs like ' 1kb' that previously failed the match and returned parseInt(' 1kb') = 1 now return 1024 (and strings like 'foo 1kb' return 1024 instead of null), which is caller-observable.

cases.note: The parse regexp lost the '+' quantifier (\d+(?:\.\d+)? became \d(?:\.\d+)?), so values with a multi-digit integer part before a unit (e.g. '10.5kb', '100kb') no longer match and fall through to parseInt on the raw string, which drops the unit and returns plain bytes. The shipped suite only parses single-digit values ('1kb', '1.5kb') and unitless strings, so it does not catch this.

cases.note: The guard was changed from `(options && options.decimalPlaces !== undefined)` to `(options && true)`, so passing an options object without decimalPlaces yields undefined and toFixed(undefined) rounds to 0 decimals instead of the default 2. E.g. bytes(1280, {}) now returns '1KB' instead of '1.25KB', and bytes.format(1536, { unitSeparator: ' ' }) returns '2 KB' instead of '1.5 KB'.

cases.note: The file is behaviourally identical to bytes@3.1.2: the unit map, both format regexes, format()'s unit-selection/decimal-stripping/thousands-separator logic, and parse()'s isNaN guard with Math.floor (e.g. parse('0.9kb') === 921, parse('nan') === null, format(1024) === '1KB') all match the released tag. No caller-observable behaviour change, so this is an equivalent refactor/no-op.

The `type === 'string'` guard was replaced with `true`, so any value with a `length > 0` (arrays, String objects) is coerced and parsed instead of throwing, and `ms(null)`/`ms(undefined)` now dereference `.length` and throw a TypeError rather than the documented Error. Both differences are caller-observable; the bundled suite does not exercise these inputs.

cases.note: The only change versus ms@2.1.3 is an added `case '':` in the minutes fall-through of the switch in parse(). It is unreachable dead code: the regex unit group can only capture a non-empty unit or be undefined, and `(match[2] || 'ms')` maps undefined (or any empty string) to 'ms', so `type` is never '' and behaviour is identical for all inputs.

The if/else unit chain was replaced by an equivalent multipliers lookup table: all 31 unit keys map to the same multipliers as the original chain, the hasOwnProperty guard always passes for regex-matched units, and n*1 === n reproduces the direct millisecond return. All other code is unchanged, so behavior is identical to ms@2.1.3.
